newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Polynesia president faces corruption trial.
newsitem.headline: French Polynesia president faces corruption trial.

text.p: A Paris appeals court on Monday ordered the president of French Polynesia's territorial government, Gaston Flosse, who is a close ally of President Jacques Chirac, to stand trial on corruption charges.

Flosse, 65, is suspected of pocketing about one million francs ($200,000) in bribes from illegal gambling operations in Papeete and Pirae, paid between 1988 and 1992 in exchange for protection from prosecution, justice officials said.
Flosse, who accompanied Chirac this month on an official visit to Japan, was mayor of Pirae at the time the bribes were allegedly paid.
If convicted, he could face up to 10 years in prison.
Four other individuals, including three associates of Floss, were also ordered to stand trial by the appeals court.
Flosse said last year that he had been cleared in a dozen corruption probes, adding that two remained open. He did not go into details.
Flosse, who was re-elected president of French Polynesia's territorial assembly last May, refers to Chirac as "my brother".

A member of Chirac's Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) party, Flosse was an outspoken supporter of France's last series of nuclear tests in the South Pacific, which ended in January sparking outrage in French Polynesia and the rest of the world.
Justice officials say that several dozen French Polynesian politicians are now under investigation in corruption cases.
Such probes are handled in Paris under a special arrangement. ($1=5.118 French Franc)
